Job description:

 
Help sustain Tasmania's volunteer emergency response capability.

 

 






 
The Team

Reporting to the Manager of Community Responders and Volunteers, you will have a statewide role in administrative responsibility for all Ambulance Tasmania volunteers and the GoodSAM community responder program.

You will engage with and support the three regional Volunteer and Responder Team Leaders.

The Role

Ambulance Tasmania is seeking a dedicated individual for the role of Volunteer and Community Responder Support Officer. This crucial position upholds service standards and provides essential support to our volunteer workforce and our GoodSAM community responder program. If you are passionate about championing and supporting volunteers, we encourage you to apply.

The Volunteer and Community Responder Support Officer provides specialised volunteer-focused administrative and operational coordination support to Ambulance Tasmania's volunteer and community responder capability.

The role supports the recruitment, onboarding, coordination, retention and sustainment of Volunteer Ambulance Officers (VAOs), GoodSAM Community Responders and the GoodSAM AED Registry.

Through effective administration and coordination support of these programs, the position contributes to the availability, readiness and sustainment of frontline volunteer and community responder resources, supporting Ambulance Tasmania's operational service delivery and community resilience.

The role operates under general direction within established policies, systems and procedures and is required to follow defined processes, apply sound administrative judgement within scope, and escalate complex or sensitive matters as appropriate while maintaining a high level of confidentiality.

You will need

Act as the first point of contact for enquiries relating to volunteers, volunteering, GoodSAM community responders and related routine matters, providing standard information and guidance in a professional, sensitive and confidential manner, and referring complex or sensitive matters as appropriate.

Provide administrative support for Volunteer Ambulance Officer (VAO) lifecycle activities, including recruitment, onboarding, induction, records management and ongoing administration, in accordance with established processes and recognising the requirements of a volunteer emergency service workforce.

Provide administrative support for the GoodSAM Community Responder program, including responder screening, onboarding, communications and routine coordination activities in accordance with established procedures.

Job description:

 
Provide friendly administrative and reception support to help deliver high-quality healthcare services to the community.

 

 






 

The Team

Midlands Multipurpose Health Centre (MMPHC) is located in Oatlands, one hour north of Hobart. MMPHC is a 22-bed medical centre, which includes 18 aged care beds and 4 rural health (acute- sub-acute) beds. There is also a 24-7 emergency care centre. All our services work closely with THS South to focus on delivering excellence in healthcare to achieve improved outcomes for our consumers, our workforce, and the Tasmanian community.

The Role

Support the efficient and effective flow of information within MMPHC by providing administrative and clerical support on a day-to-day basis to management and staff, 7 days a week (inclusive of public holidays)

Provide an efficient and friendly client focused, information and reception service, ensuring prompt, sensitive and confidential handling of enquiries

Maintain central filing systems including daily filing, data entry, retrieval of documents and archiving of records in accordance with established guidelines.

You will need

Demonstrated ability to perform administrative and organisational support duties with a basic knowledge of financial administration procedures which includes purchasing goods and services, coding of invoice payments and GST processes.

Demonstrated understanding of, and experience in, maintaining client confidentiality and the privacy of client information within a health care setting.

Good written and interpersonal skills including the ability to understand the needs of frail and aged adults and communicate effectively with multidisciplinary staff, clients and their families.

Note: - Please refer to the Statement of Duties for all the selection criteria of this position to address in your application.

Why Tasmania

The Department of Health Tasmania oversees various hospitals across the state, including the Royal Hobart Hospital, Launceston General Hospital, Northwest Regional Hospital, and Mersey Community Hospital, as well as district hospitals and ambulance services. Additionally, it provides community health, mental health, and primary healthcare services to the Tasmanian community through more than 300 sites.

Tasmania, Australia's only island state, offers unparalleled natural beauty and a luxurious lifestyle. Pursuing your health career in Tasmania's public health system means building strong connections with colleagues and patients. It also means embracing a lifestyle where you can enjoy extraordinary experiences outside of work while making a significant impact on the community during work.

UNI-SPAN HEIGHT SAFETY PTY LTD is the Australian entity of the broader Uni-Span Group, a specialist in formwork and scaffolding solutions for construction and infrastructure projects. Operating since at least 2006, the company provides and hires out Quickstage scaffolding systems, custom formwork solutions, and engineering support, serving industries such as civil, commercial, and power generation.

We are seeking skilled and qualified Scaffolders to join our team in NSW and QLD.

The role includes but is not limited to:
Determining job requirements and planning/configuring scaffolding
Undertake checking and assessing activities of scaffold prior to, during and at the completion of each build
Erecting lifting tackles by attaching pulleys and blocks to fixed overhead structures, and installing cables and attaching counterweights
Attaching slinging gear to hoisting equipment and objects to be moved using clamps, hooks, bolts and knots
Fitting and bolting tubes, support braces and components to form bases and build up scaffolding
Lifting and positioning sections of scaffolding
Carry out tasks within agreed time limits
Dismantling and removing on completion
Carry out tasks within agreed time limits
Fixing mesh and reinforcing steel into position in formwork for concrete pours
Setting up winches and rigging equipment to raise and position girders, plates, columns and other steel units
Erecting guard rails, guy wires, ropes and clears, laying planks and hanging safety nets
Help identify hazards, defects and the need for adjustment or repair; to ensure compliance with agreed codes, law, working practices and health and safety
Maintain accurate records of inspection and hand over
Where possible, rectify identified defects, failures, errors or omissions to scaffold structures. If not possible ensure reporting to the required personnel and restrict access to structure until such time the defect is rectified
Adhere to all organisational and customer policies, procedures and Safety Health Management System requirements
Ensure all scaffold, temporary works and other scaffold related activities are undertaken in accordance with Australian Standards and the relevant states Code of Practice

To be considered for this role, you must have the following:
Demonstratable working experience of at least 3 years in a similar role within the Construction and Maintenance industries
High Risk Work Licence (SB, SI or SA)
Proven experience erecting, maintaining and dismantling Scaffolding structures in the Port, Coal, Construction and Maintenance industries
Working at Heights Competency
Confined Space Entry Competency
Gas Test Atmospheres Competency
Coal Board Medical and Standard 11 Induction Competency
Desirable: Any or combination of Work Platform (WP), Forklift Truck (LF), Intermediate Rigger (RI), Dogger (DG) or Non-Slew Crane (CN) High Risk Work Licence/s
Construction Industry Induction – Blue/White Card
Ability to work well both independently and in a team environment
Strong communication skills
Strong commitment to hassle free customer service
Strong commitment to health, safety, environment and compliance standards
Willingness to work extended hours, shift work or hours as required to achieve positive outcomes
Desire to lead a highly driven team to achieve successful outcomes for both the customer and in turn, MI Scaffold
Self-motivated, organised, punctual and reliable
Must have great work ethics

If you meet the above criteria and would like to be considered for this position, please apply now!
Salary: Between $79,499 and $82,000 per annum + Super

result.description: R2 Sheetmetal & Fabrication Pty Ltd   Construction Estimator     R2 Sheet Metal & Fabrication Pty Ltd  Construction Estimator at Sheet Metal & Fabrication Pty Ltd is responsible for preparing accurate and competitive cost estimates for mechanical ductwork projects. The role involves reviewing engineering plans, specifications, and tender documents to determine project scope, performing detailed quantity take-offs and costings using Autodesk Est MEP, and sourcing and evaluating supplier and subcontractor quotations to ensure cost efficiency.  The position also includes preparing and submitting tender proposals within strict deadlines, identifying cost-saving opportunities, and assessing financial risks associated with bids. The Estimator works closely with the Managing Director, Operations Manager, and clients to ensure estimates accurately reflect project requirements and commercial expectations.  In addition, the role supports the updating and sourcing of cost databases, managing tender documentations and correspondences, and follows up on submitted bids to improve project award success rates. It also assists the operations team with ductwork fabrication data preparation using Autodesk CAMDuct, contributing to smooth project delivery from estimation through production planning. Proven experience in estimating, cost planning, or tender preparation within HVAC, ductwork or sheet metal manufacturing.  Strong ability to read and interpret mechanical drawings, technical specifications, and tender documents to prepare accurate quantity take-offs and cost estimates.  Proficiency in estimating and design software such as Autodesk Est MEP, with familiarity in Autodesk CAMDuct or similar fabrication/estimating tools.  Strong analytical and numerical skills with the ability to assess material, labour, and subcontractor costs, while identifying cost-saving and value engineering opportunities.  Excellent communication and coordination skills, with the ability to liaise effectively with management, clients, suppliers, and internal teams to ensure accurate and competitive tender submissions.      About Company    R2 Sheet Metal and Fabrication is a business located at Ottoway South Australia.       Work Type:  Full time   Salary:  $76000-86000   Job Publish:  29-06-2026   Job Expire:  29-07-2026   Apply Link:  https://workinitiatives.com.au/job/details?id=5933921   This job is brought to you by workinitiatives.com.au.

result.description:
MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Supported Living Facilitator-Planning and Admin|QCSS

Employment Term:Permanent Full Time

Located in:Annerley

Remuneration:$34.58p-hr+Super + NFP Salary Packaging (save tax and increase your take home pay)

Applications will be reviewed as they arereceived, andtherefore may result in the role closing early if the right applicant is found.

Make a meaningful difference with UnitingCare Queensland 

AtUnitingCarewe are leaders in crisis response, the protection of vulnerable people and children, financialresilienceand family wellbeing. OurFaDS(Family and Disability Services) teamworkpassionately across Queensland to make a meaningful difference in people's lives.

As aSupported Living Facilitator- Planning and Admin,you'llbe encouraged to grow,developand feel empowered to make the everyday easier for the people we care so passionately about. Let'smake a meaningful difference, together!

Your part in our UnitingCare team

You'llsupportpeoplelivingwithdisability to live meaningful lives through person-centred planning, community connection and coordinated administrative support. The role contributes to the delivery of high-quality, compliant services byfacilitatingindividual plans, supporting daily living outcomes, and undertaking administrative and record-keeping functions that enable effective service delivery.You will:

Provide support to people in their everyday living situations, including personal care asidentified, with a strong emphasis on choice, enhancing quality of life,healthand wellbeing, whilst ensuing duty of care is always upheld

In conjunction with program leadership - develop, implement, and review individual plans of the person being supported.

Assistpeople to fulfil valued community roles through engagement with community groups, potential employers and suitable programs or activities.

Advocate for andfacilitatewarm referrals tosuiableservices to address client needs outside the scope of the program.

Undertake a range of administrative functions that directly support service delivery and individual outcomes,including:basic financial and transactional activities,data capture, documentation and reporting related to case management,monitoringand supporting compliance with organisational,fundingand legislative requirements.

Undertake other administrative duties such as reception back up whenrequired

Contribute to an environment of excellence and drive for positive outcomes

What makes a difference for us? 

Able to work effectively with others in a team-oriented environment and provide excellent support to clients and co-workers

Able to effectively communicate in spoken and written English

Relevant certification anddemonstratedexperience in theDisabilitysector

Awareness of legislation underpinning the provision of services within theDisabilitysector and the key issues affecting quality of life for people with a Disability

A current NDIS Worker screening check 

Current CPR and First Aid Certificate (requiredbefore you start) 

What makes a difference for you?

Flexible work arrangements to support work-life balance 

NFP Salary Packaging: Save tax and increase your take home pay by salary packaging your everyday living expenses and bills (up to $15,900) and meal entertainment (up to $2,650) per annum. To learn more about this benefit watch the video via the following link: Salary Packaging Explained 

A recognition and rewards platform, providing employee discounts at hundreds of retailers, including everyday expenses, holidays, health insurance, annual awards celebration, wellbeing and employee assistance programs 

12 weeks paid parental leave and 2 weeks paid partner leave, available after 6 months service, in addition to the government scheme 

Diversity and inclusive leave, offering paid gender affirmation leave and cultural leave options (paid and unpaid) for those who may celebrate Lunar New Year, Diwali, Ramadan, NAIDOC weeks and other significant cultural events 

Career development opportunities to challenge yourself, grow and make a meaningful difference 

A positive and inclusive team based on respect, shared standards, strong values and a commitment to serving others 

We'd love you to be part of our UnitingCare family 

Joining our FaDS, team, you'll also be welcomed as part of the UnitingCare family. The second-largest Queensland employer, we're a proud not-for-profit with more than 16,500 staff and 9,000 volunteers across our brands of BlueCare, Lifeline, ARRCS, The Wesley Hospital, Buderim Private Hospital, St Stephen's Hospital, and St Andrew's War Memorial Hospital, and have been leading by example for more than 100 years. 

Child safe, Child friendly 

UnitingCare is committed to being a Child Safe, Child Friendly organisation and will: 

provide welcoming, safe and nurturing services for children 

implement measures to prevent child abuse and neglect within our services 

appropriately and immediately address child abuse and neglect if it does occur 

abide by the Child Safe Standards and adhere to the Reportable Conduct Scheme 

Diversity & Inclusion 

Our approach is simple - everybody is welcome here. At UnitingCare, diversity is at the core of our who we are, our mission and our values. We are committed to providing equal opportunities to all employees no matter their sex, race, culture, sexual orientation, disability or gender identity. Demonstrating our commitment to reconciliation and building long-term employment opportunities for First Nations peoples, UnitingCare strongly encourages Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander applicants for this position. 

Safe workplace 

We work hard to make our services welcoming and safe for every person. We are united in keeping children, young people and the elderly safe from harm, within our services, workplaces and the communities we support. We are committed to speaking up loudly for their safety. 

Commitment to Safeguarding

We are committed in creating services and workplaces that are welcoming and safe for every person. We work together to protect children, young people, adults and the elderly from harm within our services and the communities we support. We speak up for their safety to ensure their voices are heard. Our recruitment and workplace practices reflect our dedication in preventing abuse, harm and exploitation across UnitingCare.    Click here to Apply now →
